headline: Strong pricing drives sharp profit growth as margins widen
summary_short: CF Industries reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $2,222M, up 17.6% y/y and 11.9% q/q, with diluted EPS of $4.73 (+99.6% y/y) as strong nitrogen pricing lifted gross margin to 51.5% of sales and Adjusted EBITDA to $1,192M.
summary_long: Adjusted EBITDA rose to $1,192M (+56.6% y/y) as a $588M pricing gain outweighed a $158M volume headwind and a $52M swing in business-interruption insurance. Net earnings attributable to common stockholders reached $727M ($4.73 diluted EPS), nearly double last year. CF returned $302M to shareholders in Q2 via $225M of buybacks and dividends, then raised its quarterly dividend 20% to $0.60/share in July. Blue Point's low-carbon ammonia JV received permits in July, with construction starting in August; Yazoo City remains offline pending a 1H 2027 restart. Management guides FY2026 CF-funded capex to ~$950M (~$400M for Blue Point) and gross ammonia production to ~9.5 million tons.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes the gain to a tight global nitrogen supply-demand balance and strong realized pricing, partly offset by lower sales volumes.
Company's own bridge shows a $588M favorable pricing swing outweighing a $158M unfavorable volume impact and a $52M unfavorable swing in business-interruption insurance versus Q2 2025.
Margin expansion is arithmetically explained by net sales growing faster than cost of sales; the natural-gas cost used in production was roughly flat y/y ($3.36 to $3.37/MMBtu).
Growth mirrors the Adjusted EBITDA increase from higher realized pricing; the release does not separately explain net-earnings drivers beyond the EBITDA bridge.
EPS growth reflects both higher net earnings and a lower diluted share count (153.9M vs 163.1M a year ago) from continued buybacks.
not explained in the release beyond forward guidance for the full year (~$950M FY2026 CF-funded capex, ~$400M for Blue Point).

Company frames the quarter as outstanding operational performance amid tight global nitrogen supply-demand fundamentals, citing 98% 1H available-ammonia-capacity utilization and capacity utilization ahead of North American peers.
